steps: Start by cooking the rice. Rinse the rice in a sieve and cook in a large pan of boiling water for 25 mins, or according to package instructions.
Preheat a non-stick frying pan over a high heat and prepare your chosen vegetables (spinach, carrot, bean sprouts).

Add 1 tsp oil to the pan and add your first vegetable, allowing it to cook until softened and warm; lightly season each with a drizzle of soy sauce. Cook the vegetables in this order: carrots, bean sprouts, spinach, adding each to the pan at intervals and cooking together, seasoning with soy sauce.

On a high heat, add 1 tsp oil to the same pan as used for the vegetables, add the bulgogi beef, and stir-fry until cooked to your liking or warmed through. Season with soy sauce and set aside until ready.
On a high heat, add another tsp of oil to the pan and swirl around. Crack the egg into a small ramekin and gently pour into the pan.
Turn down to a medium-high heat, put a lid on, and allow to cook for 2 minutes or until the white is set and the yolk is runny.
While the egg is cooking, put the rice in the bottom of a bowl and arrange the vegetables and beef around the bowl. Once the egg is cooked, place it on top of the rice bowl.
Add the gochujang and a drizzle of sesame oil as toppings.
The Korean way is to break the yolk and mix everything together — the runny yolk coats the rice grains and vegetables, making a delicious dish that is best enjoyed with a spoon.
Place the chicken breast in a small pot with sliced ginger, scallion whites, and a pinch of salt, then cover with cold water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Poach for 15-18 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, then lift out and set aside, keeping the poaching broth in the pot.
Skim off any excess fat, add the jasmine rice to the broth, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
While the rice cooks, slice the cucumber into batons and slice the chicken once it is cool enough to handle.
Fluff the rice, plate it with the chicken and cucumber, and scatter over the sliced scallion greens.
Spoon a little of the extra poaching broth over the top before serving.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the spätzle according to packet instructions, then drain well.
Return the spätzle to the pot over low heat and stir in the grated Emmental in two batches, letting each batch melt before adding the next.
Once the cheese is fully melted and coats the spätzle, divide between four warm plates.
Scatter the fried onions over the top of each portion.
Toss the mixed salad leaves with the vinaigrette and serve alongside the käsespätzle.
Heat the vegetable stock in a pan and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat, add the chopped onion, and cook for 3-4 minutes until soft.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for 4-5 minutes until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Stir in the arborio rice and toast for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring frequently and letting each addition absorb before adding the next, for about 18-20 minutes until the rice is creamy and just tender.
Remove from the heat, stir through the grated parmesan, and serve immediately.
Heat a splash of oil in a large pot and cook the diced carrot and courgette for 4-5 minutes until starting to soften.
Stir in the ras el hanout and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the drained chickpeas, chopped tomatoes, and chopped dried apricots, then simmer for 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile, cover the couscous with an equal volume of boiling water, cover the bowl, and leave for 5 minutes off the heat.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and divide between four bowls.
Spoon the tagine over the couscous to serve.
Rinse the red lentils and cook the basmati rice according to packet instructions in a separate pan.
In a large pot, cook the chopped onion and garlic in a little oil for 3-4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the turmeric and cumin and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils and enough water to cover by about 3cm, bring to the boil, then simmer for 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils break down and thicken.
Stir in the chopped tomato and spinach, and cook for a further 2-3 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Serve the dal spooned over the basmati rice.
Cook the basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Heat a little oil in a large pan and cook the chopped onion for 4-5 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the garam masala and cook for 30 seconds, then add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the drained chickpeas and simmer for 8-10 minutes, mashing a few against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Season to taste and serve over the basmati rice.
Cook the basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Cut the paneer into cubes and fry in a little oil for 3-4 minutes until golden on a couple of sides, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the chopped onion for 4-5 minutes until soft, then stir in the curry spices and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped tomatoes and mixed vegetables, and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Return the paneer to the pan and simmer for a further 3-4 minutes to heat through.
Serve over the basmati rice.
Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and mix with 1 tbsp of the yogurt, half the garam masala, and the garlic and ginger, then leave to marinate while you prepare the rest.
Cook the basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the marinated chicken for 5-6 minutes until browned on all sides.
Add the remaining garam masala, the tomato sauce, and the remaining yogurt, then simmer for 12-15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Check the chicken is no longer pink in the middle before serving.
Serve over the basmati rice.
Cook the jasmine rice according to packet instructions.
Heat a little oil in a pan and fry the sliced chicken thigh for 4-5 minutes until browned.
Stir in the green curry paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the green beans and pepper and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the fish sauce and serve over the jasmine rice.
Arrange the sushi rolls on a plate.
Pour the tamari into a small dish for dipping.
Add a small mound of pickled ginger to the side of the plate.
Steam or microwave the edamame for 2-3 minutes if frozen, then season lightly with salt.
Serve the edamame alongside the sushi with the tamari and pickled ginger.
Cook the white rice according to packet instructions.
Warm the black beans in a small pan over low heat.
Grill or pan-fry the chicken breast for 5-6 minutes per side until cooked through, then slice or shred it.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan or over a low flame for 20-30 seconds per side until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, rice, and black beans, then top with salsa, a squeeze of lime, and sliced avocado.
Serve immediately while warm.
Toss the shrimp with the cumin, chilli powder, and a pinch of salt.
Heat a little oil in a pan and cook the shrimp for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque throughout.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for 20-30 seconds per side.
Mix the plain yogurt with a squeeze of lime to make a quick dressing, then toss it through the cabbage slaw.
Fill the tortillas with the shrimp, dressed slaw, and sliced avocado.
Squeeze over extra lime and serve immediately.
Toss the sliced chicken breast with the fajita seasoning.
Heat a little oil in a large pan or skillet over high heat and fry the chicken for 5-6 minutes until browned and cooked through, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the sliced peppers and onion for 5-6 minutes until softened and lightly charred.
Return the chicken to the pan and toss together for 1-2 minutes to combine and reheat.
Warm the flour tortillas in a dry pan or microwave for a few seconds each.
Serve the chicken and pepper mixture in the tortillas with salsa and a side salad.
